items.title: Duke Energy Florida aplica la tercera reducción de tarifas para bajar las facturas de los clientes residenciales en aproximadamente un 25% en 2026
items.summary: Duke Energy Florida aplicará su tercera reducción de tarifas de 2026 entre junio y septiembre, lo que reducirá las facturas de los clientes residenciales en aproximadamente 50 dólares, o un 25 %, por cada 1,000 kilovatios-hora (kWh) de energía consumida en comparación con enero.

items.title: Ahead of hurricane season, Duke Energy Foundation awards $500,000 to strengthen storm preparedness across North Carolina
items.summary: With the 2026 hurricane season starting on June 1, the Duke Energy Foundation is awarding $500,000 to 20 organizations that are preparing communities across North Carolina for storms, while also strengthening their resiliency and capacity for safe, coordinated recovery.

items.title: New Duke Energy program helps South Carolina nonresidential customers lower costs while supporting a growing grid
items.summary: The Public Service Commission of South Carolina has approved the launch of a new nonresidential demand response program that leverages customer storage assets as flexible grid resources while delivering direct value to participating customers. By enrolling a qualifying energy storage system, customers can earn bill credits while helping support a more reliable grid during periods of high demand as the Carolinas continue to grow.

items.title: Ahead of hurricane season, Duke Energy Foundation awards $130,000 to 10 organizations advancing storm preparedness and community resiliency
items.summary: With the 2026 hurricane season starting on June 1, the Duke Energy Foundation is awarding $130,000 to 10 organizations that are preparing communities across Florida for storms, while also strengthening their resiliency and capacity for safe, coordinated recovery.

items.title: Duke Energy Florida completes solar energy site in Sumter County, estimates $250 million in customer savings over its service lifetime
items.summary: Duke Energy Florida recently announced the completion of the Jumper Creek Solar Complex in Sumter County. The site is part of the company’s plan to build 900 megawatts (MWs) of solar power in Florida by the end of 2028.

items.title: Duke Energy invests in North Carolina veterans’ career pathways through America250 grants
items.summary: As Memorial Day approaches, the Duke Energy Foundation is awarding $45,800 to three nonprofit organizations honoring and supporting North Carolina veterans.

items.title: Duke Energy Foundation honors South Carolina veterans this Memorial Day with $30,000 in grants for workforce development
items.summary: As communities honor the sacrifices of U.S. service members and their families this Memorial Day, the Duke Energy Foundation is awarding $30,000 to South Carolina nonprofit organizations who focus on the needs of veterans through the second round of funding as part of its America250 initiative. The grants – part of a total investment of more than $550,000 in the Palmetto State – have been awarded to Upstate Warrior Solution and Hidden Wounds and will help expand workforce development programs for veterans across eight counties.

items.title: Duke Energy Foundation awards $50,000 to organizations honoring and supporting Florida veterans
items.summary: As Memorial Day approaches, the Duke Energy Foundation is awarding $50,000 to five nonprofit organizations honoring and supporting Florida veterans.

items.title: Duke Energy Foundation Invests Over $250,000 to Support Veterans’ Career Pathways Across 6 States
items.summary: Through its America250 initiative, the Duke Energy Foundation is awarding 20 grants to nonprofit organizations across Duke Energy’s six-state service area, along with an investment in the United Service Organizations (USO).

items.title: Unlocking more capacity with grid-enhancing technologies
items.summary: As demand for electricity grows, Duke Energy is finding new ways to deliver more from the grid customers rely on every day.

items.title: Duke Energy breaks ground on Cayuga Energy Complex project in Vermillion County
items.summary: Duke Energy broke ground on its new project that will modernize and expand power generation at the existing Cayuga power plant in Vermillion County. Once complete, the project will increase generating capacity at Cayuga by 470 megawatts to a total of 1,476 megawatts – that’s enough to power 1.1 million homes in the company’s Indiana service area.

items.title: 90-degree heat on the way: Take these steps now to keep your home comfortable and manage energy use
items.summary: Temperatures are expected to climb into the 90s in the coming days – and with humidity, it may feel closer to 95-100°F in parts of the Carolinas. For many customers, this may be the first time cooling systems are put to the test this season, causing them to run longer to maintain indoor comfort. Warm overnight temperatures can add to the strain, keeping systems running for extended periods. Duke Energy is encouraging customers to act now with simple steps and tools that can make a difference before the hottest days arrive – especially as spring’s dry conditions and high pollen levels may already be restricting airflow for some outdoor units.

items.title: Qualified Duke Energy Florida Customers Can Get Help with Bills
items.summary: As the summer season approaches and energy usage reaches its peak, Duke Energy Florida reminds customers of its Payment Assistance Finder, a tool to connect customers with bill assistance.

items.title: Duke Energy applies for Department of Energy loans that represent potentially billions of dollars in customer savings
items.summary: DOE financing is expected to save Duke Energy customers money through lower financing costs.

items.title: Duke Energy Florida celebrates FAMU partnership, highlights customer savings during Rattler Renewable Energy Center unveiling in Hernando County
items.summary: Today, Duke Energy Florida held a ribbon cutting ceremony to officially unveil the Rattler Renewable Energy Center in Hernando County.

items.title: Powering reliability: Twelve Duke Energy Indiana lineworkers earn spot in International Lineman’s Rodeo this fall
items.summary: Duke Energy lineworkers from Indiana advanced from a regional rodeo to represent the company at the International Lineman’s Rodeo in the fall, where they will compete against top lineworkers from around the world.

items.title: Duke Energy announces dividend payments to shareholders
items.summary: Duke Energy today declared a quarterly cash dividend on its common stock of $1.065 per share.

items.title: Duke Energy reports first-quarter 2026 financial results
items.summary: Duke Energy has posted its first-quarter 2026 financial results in a news release available on the company's website: duke-energy.com/investors.

items.title: Duke Energy finalizes two initiatives to deliver more than $5 billion in cost-saving benefits to customers
items.summary: Duke Energy is committed to providing safe and reliable energy at the lowest possible cost and is delivering on that promise with more than $5 billion in cost-saving benefits to the customers and communities it serves.

items.title: Powering a community forward: Robinson Nuclear Plant and a legacy secured until 2050
items.summary: For more than five decades, Robinson Nuclear Plant has been a steady presence in Hartsville, South Carolina.

items.title: South Carolina customers projected to benefit from billions in long-term savings from approved combination of Duke Energy utilities
items.summary: South Carolina customers are projected to benefit from billions of dollars in savings over time after the Public Service Commission of South Carolina approved a settlement on Duke Energy’s proposed combination of Duke Energy Carolinas and Duke Energy Progress, an agreement designed to deliver measurable, trackable customer savings backed by shareholder guarantees.

items.title: Duke Energy Foundation invests $275,000 in nonprofits supporting Floridians’ most essential needs
items.summary: The Duke Energy Foundation is awarding $275,000 to 15 nonprofit organizations that are helping meet Floridians’ most basic, essential needs and increasing access to quality health care, affordable housing, workforce development and more.

items.title: Duke Energy commits $1 million to strengthen nonprofits helping North Carolina customers meet essential needs
items.summary: The Duke Energy Foundation is committing $1 million to support nonprofits across North Carolina that deliver critical community services, including housing stability, food access, health care, utility assistance and more.

items.title: Robinson Nuclear Plant receives approval from U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission to continue operating until 2050
items.summary: Located in Hartsville, S.C., Robinson provides enough energy to power 570,000 homes and plays an important role in protecting reliability and affordability for customers as regional electricity demand continues to grow.

items.title: Duke Energy invests nearly $620,000 to strengthen North Carolina’s natural spaces, resilience and community pride this Earth Day
items.summary: Duke Energy Foundation is investing nearly $620,000 in grants to support conservation, environmental resilience and local park projects as part of Earth Day and America250 efforts

items.title: Duke Energy Florida’s tree care practices earn 20th consecutive year of national recognition
items.summary: The Arbor Day Foundation has recognized Duke Energy Florida as a “Tree Line USA” utility for the 20th year in a row for its tree care practices and environmental contribution.

items.title: Duke Energy Foundation announces first round of America250 grants to strengthen and protect South Carolina green spaces
items.summary: To strengthen communities across South Carolina as the nation approaches its 250th anniversary, Duke Energy Foundation is awarding $275,000 to organizations through a first round of funding as part of its America250 initiative. The grants – part of a total investment of more than $550,000 in the Palmetto State – will help revitalize parks and shared green spaces, support tree planting, trail maintenance and litter prevention.

items.title: Powering Reliability: Duke Energy lineworkers sharpen skills at Carolinas Lineman’s regional rodeo
items.summary: Duke Energy lineworkers from across the Carolinas advanced from a regional rodeo over the weekend to represent the company at the International Lineman’s Rodeo in October in Bonner Springs, Kan., where they will compete against top lineworkers from around the world.

items.title: Duke Energy honors South Carolina lineworkers who help restore power and build the energy grid of the future
items.summary: On April 18, Duke Energy recognizes National Lineworker Appreciation Day and the lineworkers who keep the lights on across South Carolina. From year-round grid work that improves reliability to storm response, lineworkers bring skill, teamwork and a strong safety focus to the work customers depend on. To help grow the workforce in the Palmetto State, Duke Energy Foundation is granting $75,000 to programs in South Carolina that train tomorrow’s lineworkers.

items.title: Duke Energy Foundation announces first round of America250 grants to strengthen Florida communities
items.summary: To strengthen communities across Florida as the nation approaches its 250th anniversary, the Duke Energy Foundation is awarding $22,500 to five nonprofit organizations through its America250 initiative.

items.title: Beyond Storm Response: Lineworkers making the system upgrades customers depend on
items.summary: Lineworkers do far more than storm restoration, working year-round behind the scenes to maintain, strengthen and modernize the grid so communities have safer, more reliable power now and in the future.

items.title: Ahead of Earth Day, Duke Energy Foundation announces first round of America250 grants to revitalize local parks and green spaces
items.summary: This initial grantmaking reflects the Duke Energy Foundation’s broader America250 commitment, with additional investments in veterans’ workforce development and civics education to follow later this spring.

items.title: Duke Energy outlines steps to reliably serve record customer demand resulting from extreme winter weather
items.summary: Duke Energy has filed requests with the North Carolina Utilities Commission (NCUC) related to fuel and purchased power costs incurred during one of the most extreme winter periods in the past decade – costs driven by record customer energy demand resulting from the cold weather and the utility’s commitment to keep power available and reliable when it is needed most.

items.summary: On April 18, Duke Energy recognizes National Lineworker Appreciation Day and the lineworkers who keep the lights on. From year-round grid work that improves reliability to storm response, lineworkers bring skill, teamwork and a strong safety focus to the work customers depend on.

items.summary: Duke Energy Foundation is investing $600,000 in grants to support workforce programs critical to the energy industry and local communities.

items.summary: Duke Energy (NYSE: DUK) will hold its annual shareholders meeting online on Thursday, May 7, at 1 p.m. ET.

items.title: Duke Energy and Charlotte FC team up to power communities across the Carolinas
items.summary: A new partnership between Duke Energy and Charlotte Football Club brings together the reach of professional soccer and reliable, accessible energy to deliver visible, community benefits.

items.title: Duke Energy Florida hosts Neighborhood Energy Saver Program in Clearwater
items.summary: Duke Energy Florida recently hosted its Neighborhood Energy Saver Program in Clearwater. While over 2,200 local customers are eligible to participate, approximately 75 attended the event, held at the Ross Norton Recreation Center, to learn how they can receive a free walkthrough energy assessment of their homes and help lower their monthly electricity bills.

items.title: It’s storm season in Indiana: Duke Energy’s investments in smart, self-healing technology are helping keep the lights on
items.summary: In 2025, self-healing technology helped avoid 100,000 outages for Indiana customers, saving around 350,000 hours of total outage time.

items.title: On Tampa Bay Rays Opening Day, Duke Energy Pledges Funds for Florida Customers Facing Financial Hardships Throughout the 2026 Baseball Season
items.summary: Duke Energy marks Opening Day of the Tampa Bay Rays baseball season with additional commitments to Floridians. The company and its foundation will donate $1,000 to its Share the Light Fund for every Rays regular-season game win, providing financial support to Florida customers.

items.title: Duke Energy to announce first-quarter 2026 financial results on May 5
items.summary: Duke Energy will post its first-quarter 2026 financial results at 7 a.m. ET on Tuesday, May 5, on the company’s website at duke-energy.com/investors.

items.summary: For 18 kids from Clarendon County, S.C., what wasn’t to love about their day of discovery at two of Duke Energy’s main attractions?

items.title: Ready to dig? Duke Energy, Piedmont Natural Gas remind residents to call 811 before beginning spring digging projects
items.summary: April is National Safe Digging Month, and Duke Energy and Piedmont Natural Gas are recognizing the importance of calling 811 before starting any digging projects.

items.title: Piedmont Natural Gas files application for base rate adjustment in South Carolina
items.summary: Piedmont Natural Gas today filed a request with the Public Service Commission of South Carolina to update its billing rates through a general rate case proceeding.

items.title: Duke Energy completes sale of its Tennessee Piedmont Natural Gas business to Spire
items.summary: Duke Energy today announced it has completed the sale of its Tennessee Piedmont Natural Gas business to Spire – one of the largest publicly traded natural gas companies in the country – for $2.48 billion.

items.title: Regulators approve Duke Energy’s proposal for new natural gas generation to support South Carolina’s growing energy needs
items.summary: The Public Service Commission of South Carolina (PSCSC) has approved plans by Duke Energy to construct new natural gas generation in Anderson County, a project that will help support the energy needs of a growing region while significantly contributing to the community’s economic success in the years ahead.

items.title: Energy Bill Assistance Available for Qualified Duke Energy Florida Customers
items.summary: As Duke Energy Florida’s storm cost recovery charges have been removed from customer bills as of February, dropping residential bills approximately $44 for every 1,000 kWh, additional bill assistance resources are available for eligible customers that may face continued payment challenges.

items.title: Monitor energy use with alerts - ahead of the summer heat
items.summary: As temperatures begin rising across the state, Duke Energy Florida encourages customers to explore its Usage Alerts program, a tool designed to help monitor energy use and better anticipate monthly bills before it arrives.

items.title: Duke Energy invests $500,000 to strengthen storm preparedness across North Carolina
items.summary: Duke Energy Foundation is awarding $500,000 in grants to support local storm preparedness and emergency readiness initiatives across North Carolina

items.title: Duke Energy partners with colleges to train next generation of lineworkers
items.summary: Through the Duke Energy Foundation, Duke Energy is awarding Lake-Sumter State College, Seminole State College of Florida, Valencia College, St. Petersburg College and South Florida State College each $50,000 to support their electrical lineworker training programs
